You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figures 1a and 1b, which of the following statements is most accurate about the nodule observed in the right upper lobe of this 62-year-old patient with a history of asbestos exposure?

A) The nodule is likely benign due to its smooth, well-circumscribed borders and absence of calcifications.
B) The nodule's location in the right upper lobe and well-defined edges suggest a high probability of malignancy.
C) The nodule's solitary nature and lack of associated pleural effusion indicate it is more likely a metastatic lesion.
D) The well-circumscribed appearance of the nodule and lack of calcifications suggest it is consistent with an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour.
E) The nodule's smooth borders and the absence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy suggest it is a benign hamartoma.
F) The presence of a solitary nodule in the upper lobe with these characteristics indicates it is most likely a chondroma.
